A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. The complete main text, figures, tables and Appendices A.1-A.12 are readable and can be matched despite appendix repagination.

before.justification: v2 reports original self-recognition measurements and vector-steering, projection-out and input-coloring experiments in Section 3 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including the appendix results on Sonnet 3.5, recognition without context and vectors derived from different datasets.

M1.justification: The contrastive vector construction, nuisance projection, activation steering and input-coloring procedures in Sections 2.2 and 3.2 are identical. No model or algorithm component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use CNN-DailyMail, XSUM, DOLLY, SAD and Quora QA, with the same summarization, continuation, authorship-recognition and control scenarios. Appendix coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Figures 1-2, Table 3 and the Sonnet 3.5 comparison in Appendix A.10. No comparison model or control is added or removed.

E3.justification: Sample counts, text-length normalization, paired and individual presentation protocols, accuracy metrics, model configurations and intervention settings are unchanged, including the appendix experiments.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same length and perplexity analyses, control tasks, vector-removal interventions, layer/multiplier analyses, generation examples, context-removal tests and cross-dataset vector comparisons.

E5.justification: Confidence intervals, p-value reporting and plotted error bars are unchanged, including Section 3.2.3 and Tables 1-3 and 5. No run-count, seed or uncertainty-estimation information is added or revised.

E6.justification: Tables 1-6, Figures 1-15 and qualitative generation examples retain the same results. For example, Table 1 retains chat-model accuracies of 57.2%, 61.0%, 52.3% and 65.8% for CNN, XSUM, DOLLY and SAD, respectively.

T1.justification: The mathematical descriptions of vector averaging, normalization, projection and cosine similarity are unchanged. Neither version contains a formal theorem or proof development.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and discussion retain identical claims about self-text recognition, its proposed post-training origin and control of authorship judgments through a residual-stream vector.

C2.justification: Interpretations of the vector's mechanism, possible remaining confounds, generalization beyond Llama3 and potential safety applications are unchanged. Appendix qualifications about token/order biases and degenerate outputs are also retained.

D1.justification: Sample-selection details, prompt templates, vector extraction, token positions, layers, multipliers and dataset access references are identical. The PDFs' external link destinations also match.

R1.justification: The reference list and positioning relative to prior self-recognition, activation-steering and Tuned Lens work are identical. The publication-status header does not revise the research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 adds the ICLR 2025 publication header, updates the arXiv version/date stamp and introduces a stray '%onehalfspacing' line in Appendix A.9. The substantive prose, terminology and section order otherwise match.

P2.justification: Tighter spacing beginning in Appendix A.9 reflows the remaining appendix material, moving A.10-A.12 from pages 31-33 to 30-32. Publication headers are added; figures, table contents and captions are retained without additions or removals.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, empirical evidence, interpretations and reproducibility information are identical. Publication headers and tighter appendix spacing produce no meaningful overall quality gain; the stray formatting line in A.9 is a small cosmetic defect without material impact on comprehension.
